primitives.name: Defensive-Offensive Disparity Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: Relative features are the difference between the defensive and offensive player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{r}_{ij}': 'Relative displacement vector between defender i and offense j (meters)', '\\mathbf{p}_d^{(i)}': 'Position of defender i at time t (meters)', '\\mathbf{p}_o^{(j)}': 'Position of offensive player j at time t (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player positions are measured in same reference frame; relative motion captures spatial intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When players occupy same location, \(\mathbf{r}_{ij} \to 0\), leading to numerical instability.

layer2.mapping: Encodes positional relationship between defenders and receivers for downstream classification.
layer2.telemetry: Used within CNN input tensor for frame-wise representation.

primitives.name: Team PCA Deviation Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: Uniqueness is how far a team's PCA point is from the origin.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'U': 'Uniqueness score (dimensionless)', '\\mathbf{v}_{\\text{PCA}}': "Principal component vector of team's play behavior (unitless)"}
primitives.assumptions: PCA captures dominant behavioral patterns; Euclidean norm quantifies deviation from baseline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If all plays are identical, \( U \to 0 \); high variance implies distinct strategy.

layer2.mapping: Quantifies strategic distinctiveness through PCA-based clustering of play types.
layer2.telemetry: Used in PFF analysis for identifying unique team tendencies.

reasoning_traces.think:
Coverage classification relies on a multi-stage pipeline: first, a CNN processes each frame into a feature map; next, self-attention aggregates these features across players to form a play embedding; finally, an ensemble of classifiers assigns a label among eight coverage types. This architecture leverages both spatial structure (CNN) and relational context (attention). The relative feature encoding ensures that positional disparities are captured consistently regardless of player ordering due to the 1x1 kernel convolution. The uniqueness metric computes a scalar deviation from the origin in PCA space, indicating how distinct a team's playstyle is. These primitives support robust inference under varying game states but may fail when coverage labels are ambiguous or when positional data is noisy.
